_about: Choosing Narada's planner model (2026-10-03). scripts/planner_eval.py: 19 jobs the planner exists for (8 shortcuts, 4 actions, 2 confirm cards, 2 safety, 3 artifacts), each in a throwaway house with the real planner lane, every capability and a small copy of the site, against the real NIM models. The owner's candidates were Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3; every chat model the account lists was considered.
why_not_kimi_k3_or_glm_5_3: On NIM that night both took 110-243 s (Kimi K3) and 161-171 s (GLM 5.3) before the first token of a five-word answer. A planner job is several model calls; at that speed one job takes ten minutes or times out, so they were not benchmarked on the jobs. Worth measuring again when NIM serves them faster: the eval takes --models moonshotai/kimi-k3 --timeout 400.

reading_round_4: nemotron-3-ultra 51/57, median 11.6 s; 2 of its 6 misses were NIM read timeouts (no answer in 120 s) and 3 were the eval's own fault (it did not accept owner_presence != home as leaving; fixed after the run), so on the jobs it answered it was right 54 of 55. nemotron-3-super with thinking 50/57, median 12.1 s; its misses are real (read an empty room as leaving home; retried create_shortcut up to 11 times on one job; once gave a user a card for a shortcut only an admin may make instead of saying so).

chosen.where: PLANNER_DEFAULT_MODEL / PLANNER_DEFAULT_FALLBACKS in Garuda_web.py; NIM_PLANNER_MODEL / NIM_PLANNER_FALLBACKS in .env override

lessons: More than two jobs at once trips NIM's rate limit; it shows as 'the AI service is unavailable'.
Models call tools they were not given (the old rule drafter, by name): only offered tools run now.
Offered both rules and shortcuts, models drafted both; the planner is given shortcuts only.
Measure a model before making it the default: the first default (Kimi K3) made the owner's live planner requests wait minutes.
